> This page covers caching with [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), enabled by setting [`cacheComponents: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.ts` file. If you're not using Cache Components, see the [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components) guide.

Caching is a technique for storing the result of data fetching and other computations so that future requests for the same data can be served faster, without doing the work again.

## Enabling Cache Components

00121| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher

00123| // 'auto' | 'default-cache' | 'only-cache'
00124| // 'force-cache' | 'force-no-store' | 'default-no-store' | 'only-no-store'

00126| 
00127| - **`'auto'`** (default): The default option to cache `fetch` requests before Request-time APIs with the `cache` option they provide and not cache `fetch` requests after Request-time APIs.
00128| - **`'default-cache'`**: Allow any `cache` option to be passed to `fetch` but if no option is provided then set the `cache` option to `'force-cache'`. This means that even `fetch` requests after Request-time APIs are considered static.
00129| - **`'only-cache'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt into caching by changing the default to `cache: 'force-cache'` if no option is provided and causing an error if any `fetch` requests use `cache: 'no-store'`.
00130| - **`'force-cache'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt into caching by setting the `cache` option of all `fetch` requests to `'force-cache'`.
00131| - **`'default-no-store'`**: Allow any `cache` option to be passed to `fetch` but if no option is provided then set the `cache` option to `'no-store'`. This means that even `fetch` requests before Request-time APIs are considered dynamic.
00132| - **`'only-no-store'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt out of caching by changing the default to `cache: 'no-store'` if no option is provided and causing an error if any `fetch` requests use `cache: 'force-cache'`
00133| - **`'force-no-store'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt out of caching by setting the `cache` option of all `fetch` requests to `'no-store'`. This forces all `fetch` requests to be re-fetched every request even if they provide a `'force-cache'` option.
00134| 
00135| ##### Cross-route segment behavior
00136| 
00137| - Any options set across each layout and page of a single route need to be compatible with each other.
00138|   - If both the `'only-cache'` and `'force-cache'` are provided, then `'force-cache'` wins. If both `'only-no-store'` and `'force-no-store'` are provided, then `'force-no-store'` wins. 00139|   - The intention of the `'only-*'` and `'force-*'` options is to guarantee the whole route is either fully static or fully dynamic. This means:
00140|     - A combination of `'only-cache'` and `'only-no-store'` in a single route is not allowed.
00141|     - A combination of `'force-cache'` and `'force-no-store'` in a single route is not allowed.
00142|   - A parent cannot provide `'default-no-store'` if a child provides `'auto'` or `'*-cache'` since that could make the same fetch have different behavior.

00145| </details>
00146| 
00147| ## Time-based revalidation
00148| 
00149| Use the `next.revalidate` option on `fetch` to revalidate data after a specified number of seconds:
00150| 
00151| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00152| export default async function Page() {
00153|   const data = await fetch('https://...', { next: { revalidate: 3600 } })
00154| }
00155| ```
00156| 
00157| ```jsx filename="app/page.jsx" switcher
00158| export default async function Page() {
00159|   const data = await fetch('https://...', { next: { revalidate: 3600 } })
00160| }
00161| ```
00162| 
00163| For non-`fetch` functions, `unstable_cache` accepts a `revalidate` option in its configuration (see [example above](#unstable_cache-for-non-fetch-functions)).
00164| 
00165| ### Route segment config `revalidate`
00166| 
00167| Set the default revalidation time for a layout or page. This option does not override the `revalidate` value set by individual `fetch` requests.
00168| 
00169| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
00170| export const revalidate = false
00171| // false | 0 | number
00172| ```
00173| 
00174| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
00175| export const revalidate = false
00176| // false | 0 | number
00177| ```
00178| 
00179| - **`false`** (default): The default heuristic to cache any `fetch` requests that set their `cache` option to `'force-cache'` or are discovered before a Request-time API is used. Semantically equivalent to `revalidate: Infinity` which effectively means the resource should be cached indefinitely. It is still possible for individual `fetch` requests to use `cache: 'no-store'` or `revalidate: 0` to avoid being cached and make the route dynamically rendered. Or set `revalidate` to a positive number lower than the route default to increase the revalidation frequency of a route.
00180| - **`0`**: Ensure a layout or page is always dynamically rendered even if no Request-time APIs or uncached data fetches are discovered. 00181| - **`number`**: (in seconds) Set the default revalidation frequency of a layout or page to `n` seconds.
00182| 
00183| > **Good to know**:
00184| >
00185| > - The revalidate value needs to be statically analyzable. For example `revalidate = 600` is valid, but `revalidate = 60 * 10` is not.
00186| > - The revalidate value is not available when using the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'`.
00187| > - In Development, Pages are _always_ rendered on-demand and are never cached. This allows you to see changes immediately without waiting for a revalidation period to pass.
00188| 
00189| #### Revalidation frequency
00190| 
00191| - The lowest `revalidate` across each layout and page of a single route will determine the revalidation frequency of the _entire_ route. This ensures that child pages are revalidated as frequently as their parent layouts.
00192| - Individual `fetch` requests can set a lower `revalidate` than the route's default `revalidate` to increase the revalidation frequency of the entire route. This allows you to dynamically opt-in to more frequent revalidation for certain routes based on some criteria.
00193| 
00194| ## On-demand revalidation
00195| 
00196| To revalidate cached data after an event, use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) or [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) in a [Server Action](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).

00208| ```
00209| 
00210| ```jsx filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher

00213|     next: { tags: ['user'] },
00214|   })
00215| }
00216| ```
00217| 
00218| For non-`fetch` functions, `unstable_cache` also accepts a `tags` option (see [example above](#unstable_cache-for-non-fetch-functions)).
00219| 
00220| ### `revalidateTag`
00221| 
00222| Invalidate cached data by tag using [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag):
00223| 
00224| ```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" switcher
00225| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
00226| 
00227| export async function updateUser(id: string) {
00228|   // Mutate data
00229|   revalidateTag('user', 'max')
00230| }
00231| ```
00232| 
00233| ```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" switcher
00234| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
00235| 
00236| export async function updateUser(id) {
00237|   // Mutate data
00238|   revalidateTag('user', 'max')
00239| }
00240| ```
00241| 
00242| ### `revalidatePath`
00243| 
00244| Invalidate all cached data for a specific route path using [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath):
00245| 
00246| ```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" switcher
00247| import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
00248| 
00249| export async function updateUser(id: string) {
00250|   // Mutate data
00251|   revalidatePath('/profile')

00253| ```

00259|   // Mutate data

00262| ```
00263| 
00264| ## Deduplicating requests
00265| 
00266| If you are not using `fetch` (which is [automatically memoized](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch#memoization)), and instead using an ORM or database directly, you can wrap your data access with the [React `cache`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) function to deduplicate requests within a single render pass:

00271| 
00272| export const getPost = cache(async (id: string) => {

00292| You can preload data by creating a utility function that you eagerly call above blocking requests. This lets you initiate data fetching early, so the data is already available by the time the component renders.

00298| import 'server-only'

00307| ```
